title.narrative: Study Environmental Social Governance in Ukraine

description.narrative: The results of this project will provide facts and information of the readiness of Ukrainian businesses to implement European Union (EU) Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) standards; which will further foster a more sustainable and transparent business environment in the country. It will equip public and private stakeholders with actionable insights, enabling informed decision-making and policy development. Ultimately, this study will support Ukraine's ambition for integration to the EU in alignment to the EU’s green transition goals.The project has a positive impact on:SDG 8: inclusive and sustainable economic growth: support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation.

comment.narrative:
The project directly enhanced ESG awareness and preparedness, especially among SMEs, creating conditions for more sustainable and informed business operations.
200 MSMEs took part in the quantitative survey; over 60% expressed concrete interest in aligning with ESG standards.
The study results demonstrate that although a small percentage of companies (about 7-9%) are well-informed about international ESG standards,
Readiness of Ukrainian business for change Despite the identified gaps, Ukrainian business demonstrates an impressive level of readiness for transformation.
87% have a positive attitude toward implementing ESG standards, and almost half (44%) declare their readiness to submit relevant reports in the first year after the introduction of such norms. 87% of all surveyed companies indicated that ESG tools and clear guidance would improve their capacity to implement sustainability practices. 77% of Ukrainian companies consider the shortage of qualified personnel and insufficient competence of current employees to be the biggest obstacle to implementing ESG approaches, 71% of companies complain about the lack of accessible information regarding the implementation of standards and ESG reporting.
Technological aspects also create considerable difficulties: 68% of companies recognize the collection and processing of large data sets as problematic, and 65% are concerned about the need to use specialized software.
Ukrainian companies also demonstrate an understanding of the key elements of successful transformation. About 89% are confident that employee training will significantly improve their readiness for ESG challenges. In parallel, 87% expect that the implementation of digital solutions will significantly simplify the reporting process. It is important to note that a similar percentage (86%) support the idea of a phased introduction of standards with a possible transition period, which indicates a pragmatic approach to transformation.
